root.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Semi-Tarrasch Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 d5 4. Nc3 c5

overview: Black strikes at d4 with ...c5 before castling, a more active version of the Tarrasch without the isolated pawn forced on Black. In the main line 5.cxd5 Nxd5 6.e4 Nxc3 7.bxc3 cxd4 8.cxd4 Bb4+ White gets a big centre and Black piece pressure on it; in the quieter 5.e3 Nc6 6.a3 cxd4 7.exd4 Black has an IQP-type structure. White presses with the centre and development, Black aims to attack the centre and trade pieces.

white_ideas.idea: Take on d5 and play e4 to build a big pawn centre
e3, a3 and dxc5 or exd4 for a quieter edge with the IQP
Bg5 (Pillsbury) pinning the knight and pressing against d5

black_ideas.idea: Attack the d4 pawn with ...Nc6, ...cxd4 and ...Bb4+ to prove the centre is a target
Trade pieces with ...Nxc3 and ...Bd7 to reach an easy endgame
Accept an IQP or hanging pawns in return for active piece play

typical_structures.structure: White pawn centre c3/d4/e4 against Black pieces after exchanges
Isolated queen's pawn for White after exd4

character.notes: Concrete play with tension around d4/e4 where both sides take some risk; not as sharp as the Botvinnik but not a fortress either.

soundness.notes: Sound; a main-line defence at top level.

structure.notes: Centre in tension with IQP or hanging pawns, so Flexible.

approach.notes: A mainstream defence in the QGD complex.

level.notes: Main lines with 6.e4 need known theory and IQP positions need understanding; intermediate to advanced.

sublines_that_differ.name: 5.cxd5 Nxd5 6.e4
sublines_that_differ.how: Sharper, White's big centre against Black's active pieces.

sublines_that_differ.name: Pillsbury Variation
sublines_that_differ.how: Pins the f6 knight for a more forcing game.

character.reason: Active central tension but neither forcing nor a fortress.

structure.reason: The centre stays in tension with IQP or hanging pawns.

level.reason: Needs theory in the main lines and IQP understanding but is not Najdorf-heavy.

plans.reason: Typical IQP and hanging pawn positions arise.
